Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Platform: Zoom
Attendees: Sanjay Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM); Mark Reynolds (Cloudstream VP Eng), Priya Singh (Cloudstream Security Lead), Andre Cole (Cloudstream Data Platform), Tina Wu (Cloudstream SRE)
summary: Redwood demo of request-storage toggles, redaction, ephemeral logging, and console controls. Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated for regulated shipment telemetry and wants clear retention, KMS key handling, and audit log integration. Agreed pilot and follow-ups.
topics: Security Q&A: KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — is this time still good?
[00:05] Mark (Cloudstream): Yep, all good, thanks. We want to focus on the telemetry and retention controls — especially PII redaction and how logging ties into our SIEM.
[00:12] Lina (Redwood SE): Great, we'll do a short run-through in Console and then jump to the API and Optimize suggestions. I'll show ephemeral mode and the request storage toggle.
[00:20] Priya (Cloudstream): Nice, and please show KMS workflows — we have to ensure keys never leave our boundary and logs are encrypted at rest.
[00:28] Lina (Redwood SE): Yep, we'll cover S3 storage options, KMS integration, and also the toggle that prevents request bodies from persisting.
[00:35] [screen share starts] Lina (Redwood SE): Ok, so this is the Console — under Settings -> Data Controls. Right here is the Request Storage switch. When you turn it off, we mark requests ephemeral and they are excluded from long-term request store. There is still short-lived buffering for active inference but it's TTL'd within minutes.
[00:53] Tina (Cloudstream): When you say TTL, is that configurable per-route? We have different SLAs per tenant.
[00:58] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes, per-route TTL or per API key. You can set default retention windows — 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d — and also route-level overrides. The console will show effective policy.
[01:12] Andre (Cloudstream): How does that interact with batching — if you batch requests, does it retain the raw prompts?
[01:18] Lina (Redwood SE): Good q. Batching groups incoming calls before they hit runtime; we support prefix/KV cache so you can enable prefix caching without storing full user payloads. In ephemeral mode we avoid persisting raw request bodies to the long-term store; only metadata for billing/sla is kept. There's a short lived in-memory buffer for the batch that is flushed.
[01:38] [00:01:40] Mark (Cloudstream): Ok. What about PII redaction — automated vs manual?
[01:45] Lina (Redwood SE): We have two layers: client-side redaction and server-side patterns. In Console you can set automated PII redaction rules — email, ssn, credit numbers — and you can add custom regexes per-tenant. Server-side redaction replaces matches with tokens before writing to disk. There are logs that show redaction events and counts but not the raw value.
[02:05] Priya (Cloudstream): We need proof that the redaction happened for audits. Do you keep audit logs that show original value hashes or anything?
[02:12] Sanjay (Redwood AE): We emit audit events — they include a hash fingerprint and rule id, timestamps, and who triggered the event. Those audit logs are retained per your retention policy and can be forwarded to your SIEM via our log-shipper. The original text is not stored if redaction is enabled.
[02:28] Tina (Cloudstream): Is the hash reversible?
[02:30] Sanjay (Redwood AE): No — it's a one-way SHA variant we use for tracing and de-dup without reversible PII.
[02:36] [00:02:40] Andre (Cloudstream): On KMS — can we bring our own key, rotate it, and have Redwood never store the plaintext key?
[02:44] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes, BYOK is supported. You can point to an external KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM). We support envelope encryption; the customer master key is in your control and Redwood encrypts the data key with your CMK. Key rotation is supported via policy and you can revoke access.
[03:02] Priya (Cloudstream): And the audit trail for key operations?
[03:06] Lina (Redwood SE): We surface key usage events but the canonical audit of CMK ops lives in your KMS console; we also forward a subset to the Redwood audit stream with non-sensitive metadata.
[03:16] [00:03:20] Mark (Cloudstream): Can you show me the toggle in the API — I want to be able to set this from our infra rather than the Console.
[03:24] Lina (Redwood SE): Absolutely. It's a header you can pass: x-redwood-request-visibility: ephemeral | retained. There's also a policy engine where keys or routes can default to ephemeral. Quick demo — a sample curl: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "x-redwood-request-visibility: ephemeral" -d '{"messages": [...] }'
[03:48] [00:03:50] Andre (Cloudstream): If someone forgets the header, can we enforce via policy?
[03:53] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes — policy enforcement is preferred. You can create a policy that denies retention for keys scoped to compliance tenants.
[03:59] [00:04:00] Mark (Cloudstream): What's the default for hosted customers?
[04:03] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Default is retained for usage analytics and debugging — but we set short default retention and give customers controls. For enterprise we recommend explicit policy toggles.
[04:12] Priya (Cloudstream): About log forwarding, do you support syslog, Splunk, S3, and eventstreams?
[04:18] Lina (Redwood SE): We support pushing to S3, Splunk HEC, Datadog, and we have Kafka/EventBridge connectors. For SIEM you can also use our log-shipper which signs events and forwards them.
[04:28] [00:04:30] Tina (Cloudstream): If we enable forwarding to our S3, is that encrypted with our CMK?
[04:33] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes, you can configure object encryption with your KMS key.
[04:36] [00:04:40] Mark (Cloudstream): There was a note in your docs about redaction exceptions for ML evals — can you explain?
[04:44] Lina (Redwood SE): Sure. For model-evals you can opt into storing sanitized copies of request sets for quality monitoring. We recommend using a separate eval-only bucket, masked with PII removed. There's a consent mechanism and explicit flag for those flows.
[04:58] Andre (Cloudstream): That won't leak customer PII back into model training, right?
[05:02] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Correct — no training access by default. Eval sets are stored separately, and any data used for training requires explicit opt-in and is segmented.
[05:12] [00:05:20] Priya (Cloudstream): Can we get field-level redaction? Some messages have nested JSON with addresses.
[05:18] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes, the server-side rules support JSON path patterns and you can redact nested fields by path. You can also map fields to token placeholders.
[05:28] Mark (Cloudstream): How are these rules authored? UI or API?
[05:31] Lina (Redwood SE): Both — Console rule editor has a test harness and you can import/export rules via API.
[05:36] [00:05:40] Tina (Cloudstream): For PCI-like workflows, do you recommend Hosted or Dedicated?
[05:42] Sanjay (Redwood AE): For strict PCI or regulated PII that can't be inspected by a third party we'd suggest Dedicated or Private deployment inside your VPC. Hosted with BYOK + ephemeral mode can work for many cases, but Dedicated gives you clearer isolation guarantees and predictable throughput.
[05:56] [00:06:00] Andre (Cloudstream): If we go Dedicated, do the same console controls still apply?
[06:00] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes — the same API surface and Console exist across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. The only difference is where the control plane and data plane run.
[06:10] [00:06:15] Mark (Cloudstream): Any SLA impact when we enable ephemeral mode?
[06:19] Sanjay (Redwood AE): No SLA impact by itself. However, if you enable extreme caching or very aggressive TTLs that reduce KV cache effectiveness, you may see throughput differences; we'll recommend autoscaling policies to maintain targets.
[06:36] [00:06:40] Priya (Cloudstream): Do you capture IPs in logs? We need to mask client IPs for GDPR.
[06:44] Lina (Redwood SE): Client IPs are captured as part of transport logs but we can mask or hash them on ingestion. There's a toggle for anonymize-ips.
[06:53] Tina (Cloudstream): Does anonymize affect rate-limiting or fraud detection?
[06:57] Lina (Redwood SE): It can — we offer pseudonymization instead of full anonymization when you need rate limits to remain per-client. That preserves consistent IDs without exposing raw IP.
[07:09] [00:07:10] Mark (Cloudstream): Ok, show me how we'd test this — end-to-end.
[07:12] Lina (Redwood SE): I'll flip the tenant to ephemeral and run an API call.
[07:15] [typing] Lina (Redwood SE): curl -X POST ... -H 'x-redwood-request-visibility: ephemeral' ...
[07:22] [00:07:25] Lina (Redwood SE): Response comes back, and in Console request explorer you can see the request with a redaction flag. If you click 'raw' while ephemeral is on, it will show 'not persisted' instead of raw payload.
[07:35] Andre (Cloudstream): I see. Do you keep any derived telemetry — like token counts and cost metrics?
[07:41] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Yes — we keep aggregated usage metrics for billing and to surface latency/cost breakdowns. Those are not reversible to raw prompts.
[07:52] [00:07:55] Mark (Cloudstream): About legal, if somebody in procurement asks for deletion guarantees, do you have a delete API?
[07:59] Lina (Redwood SE): We have a deletion API for request store and for embeddings. There's also a bulk-delete and a retention enforcement policy. Deletions return an audit receipt.
[08:10] Priya (Cloudstream): Is deletion eventual or synchronous? We need to certify in writing.
[08:14] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Deletion is guaranteed within policy windows; embedded indexes have compaction cycles so some derived artifacts are removed during compaction — we provide deletion receipts and timestamps for audits. We'll include exact SLAs in the security pack.
[08:26] [00:08:30] Mark (Cloudstream): Any points about costs when enabling long retention?
[08:30] Lina (Redwood SE): Longer retention increases storage + egress if you forward logs. Optimize module can recommend downsampling, TTL tiers, or storing only hashed fingerprints for older records to reduce cost.
[08:43] [00:08:45] Andre (Cloudstream): Show me Optimize suggestions for a bursty workload — we have peaks at month-end.
[08:49] Lina (Redwood SE): Optimize will analyze token distribution and recommend batching window sizes and cache hints; you can choose retention tiers per route. For bursty flows we suggest a short-term higher retention for debugging then auto-roll down to minimal retention after 48 hours.
[09:05] [00:09:10] Mark (Cloudstream): That sounds useful. Can Optimize provide an estimated cost delta?
[09:14] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes we show projected monthly cost impact when you change retention or batch size.
[09:21] [00:09:25] Priya (Cloudstream): If we run a pilot, we need a checklist: security sign-offs, sample dataset, success metrics.
[09:30] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Agreed. Typical pilot checklist: SOC2 docs review, network VPN/VPC peering or private link, KMS BYOK setup, sample prompt set and eval metrics, throughput targets for Dedicated if needed.
[09:44] [00:09:50] Mark (Cloudstream): Who from Redwood will help with onboarding?
[09:47] Jules Park (Redwood CSM): Jules here — we'll coordinate onboarding, runbook, and set up the pilot workspace. We'll also provide the sample prompts and a test harness.
[09:57] Tina (Cloudstream): On timelines — we want to start a 2-week pilot mid-March.
[09:59] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Sounds good. I'll send calendar invite for 2026-03-18 to kickoff.
[10:05] [00:10:10] Priya (Cloudstream): A couple more questions on compliance: do you support SAML SSO for console access and SCIM for user provisioning?
[10:12] Lina (Redwood SE): Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM user sync are supported. RBAC roles are customizable, and we can map groups to audit roles.
[10:20] Mark (Cloudstream): For auditors, can we export the full audit trail?
[10:23] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Yes, audit exports can be time-bounded and signed. We provide a signed export for the period you require.
[10:30] [00:10:35] Andre (Cloudstream): One nit: your docs mention KV cache — we've seen the term but sometimes it's spelled KV cash in older docs, might confuse auditors.
[10:40] Lina (Redwood SE): Oh, heh, good catch — docs team pushed a typo earlier. We'll correct that.
[10:46] [00:10:50] Mark (Cloudstream): Any competitors' caveats we should be aware of? Priya: I think Anthropic's model access approach doesn't offer BYOK in the same way.
[10:57] Priya (Cloudstream): Right — also some providers keep raw logs for 30 days by default which we can't accept.
[11:04] Sanjay (Redwood AE): We're aligned to enterprise controls here. We'll share a matrix comparing retention features vs common competitors.
[11:12] [00:11:15] Tina (Cloudstream): Ok, final quick question — embeddings retention and PII: we want to ensure embedding vectors don't leak PII.
[11:20] Lina (Redwood SE): Embeddings are stored with metadata and we support redaction at ingestion; we also offer hashing of original text and ability to delete vectors via the deletion API. For extra safety, keep embeddings in Dedicated VPC.
[11:33] [00:11:40] Mark (Cloudstream): Great. That covers most of it.
[11:36] Jules Park (Redwood CSM): Quick recap: We'll send security pack and BYOK docs, provision ephemeral demo tenant, schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-03-18, and provide runbook.
[11:50] [00:11:55] Sanjay (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials. Any last questions?
[11:58] Priya (Cloudstream): Not from me. Thanks.
[12:01] Mark (Cloudstream): Thanks all.
[12:03] [00:12:05] [call ends]
